_note: The skin. Every player-visible string lives here; mechanics live in tiles.json / items.json / search.json / events.json and never change. Names follow the vault glossary, which is the naming contract: ids are ASCII and never translated, display strings are 繁體中文 followed by English. The monster is spelled 殭屍 throughout — the 歹-radical form, never the variant with 亻.
title: The Third Watch: The Jiangshi
tagline: It is nine at night. At the third watch he comes for you. Lay him to rest, or be standing when he arrives.

lines._note: Narration. Every player-visible sentence the turn loop speaks, so a translation is a data change and never a code change. Placeholders are {braced}. Keys are named for the MOMENT, not the function that happens to call them — a translator reads this file without the source beside them.
lines.wake: You wake in the {room}. Find the {relic}{goal} before midnight.
lines.reveal: You reveal the {room} and step inside.
lines.step-out: You step out onto the {room}. Night air, and worse.
lines.cured: The grey goes out of the wound. 中毒 lifted.
lines.rite-take: The lid is not nailed down. Something in the room objects.
lines.rite-bury: You kneel and begin to dig. The ground here gives too easily.
lines.rite-aborted: You ran. What you came here to do is still undone.
lines.relic-found: Among the coffins, the {relic}. It is yours.
lines.dead-end: Nowhere on from here — until the {dir} wall gives way.
lines.breach-working: Something is working at the {dir} wall.
lines.blood-escape: You break the {item} over the floor. They lose you in it.
lines.villager-empty-handed: You have nothing to give them.
lines.search-no-room: No room for {item}. It stays where it is.
lines.use-bad-half: {item}. It was the bad half: {n} health.
lines.cinnabar-painted: You grind the {item} and paint it again. {target} ×{n}.
lines.third-watch: 三更. The drum goes, and then nothing goes at all.
lines.died-paying: You write the {item} and there is not enough of you left to finish it.
lines.start-failed: Failed to start the game — see console.
empty-handed: You turn the room over and come up with nothing.
Dust, and a drawer that was already open.
Somebody has been through here before you.
You put your hands into the dark and find the dark.
lines.strike-eleven: Eleven. The last hour — when the deck runs dry, it is midnight.
lines.warded: The stone at the junction holds. Nothing comes to this ground.
lines.search-armed: {item}. Your hand is already full — you are holding {holding}.

ui._note: Labels, the small grey line under them, and the prompts over the choice window. Kept apart from `lines` because these are things you press and those are things the house says — a translator handles them differently, and these have to stay short enough for a narrow card.
ui.moon-gate: Step out through the moon gate
ui.move-prompt: Move on or stay put — each spends six minutes.
ui.run-sub: the turn ends where you land
ui.kit-prompt: He is in the doorway. One strike — what do you show him?
ui.start-failed: Failed to start the game — see console.
ui.tablet-held: held, and it costs no slot
ui.cinnabar-lede: Paint a charm twice and it works twice. Which one — you will have {n} more of it, and a stack is still one slot.
ui.drop-lede: Your hands are full. Something has to go down before it comes up.
ui.page-title: The Third Watch: The Jiangshi — play in your browser
ui.title-calm: Calm mode — the game without the scares
ui.turns-left-none: the next turn tolls the hour
ui.attack-buffed: {item}, with 真火符 burnt into it, attack {n}
ui.title-fast: Fast mode — the beats without the animations
ui.replace-prompt: {item}. You can only hold one blade.
ui.use-elsewhere-title: Spent in the fight that needs it, not from here
ui.mode-calm-said: Calm mode is on — the 僵屍 never arrive and the scenes stay gentle. Press to turn it off.
ui.mode-fast-said: Fast mode is on — the event scenes are skipped entirely. Press to turn it off.

tileBlurbs._note: One line per tile, for the gallery. What the place is, not what it does — the mechanics come from tiles.json.
tileBlurbs.gatehouse: Where you start. Three ways on, and the gate shut behind you.
tileBlurbs.apothecary: One door. Drawers of herbs, a balance, a mortar still full.
tileBlurbs.woodshed: Poles and axes, close to the start.
tileBlurbs.sutra-hall: Scripture and talismans. The richest magic in the game.
tileBlurbs.mourning-hall: Where the coffins are laid out, under two white banners.
tileBlurbs.courtyard: The crossroads. Roofless, and its 月門 is the only way outside.
tileBlurbs.blacksmith: One door. The forge — iron is anti-yin, and the coals are still live.
tileBlurbs.counting-room: Ledgers, an abacus, and the clerk's own medicine chest behind the desk.
tileBlurbs.incense-hall: Tablets in tiers, and a coil burning down. Somewhere to stand still and let the smoke do its work.
tileBlurbs.sealed-crypt: The coffin nobody claimed, papered shut. The 神主牌 is here.
tileBlurbs.back-steps: The stone landing outside the moon gate.
tileBlurbs.dry-well: Where the village threw what it wanted gone.
tileBlurbs.bamboo-grove: Poles, and paper charms tied to them.
tileBlurbs.memorial-arch: Offerings and tools stacked at its foot.
tileBlurbs.pavilion: Somewhere to sit, if this were a different night.
tileBlurbs.pagoda-tree: 鬼樹. It heals because it is literally a medicine tree.
tileBlurbs.stone-ward: The stone at the junction, cut with its own name. Nothing comes onto this ground while it stands.
tileBlurbs.stream: 溪澗. Water over stones. Nothing to find, and nothing to keep you.
tileBlurbs.earth-god-shrine: The land god knows where the dead are buried. Ask once.
tileBlurbs.mass-grave: The pit for the unclaimed. Bury the 神主牌 here.

categories._note: The five things a room can be searched for. relic and charm hold one item each; they are categories rather than special cases so the search tables and the slot rules stay uniform.

itemBlurbs._note: One line each, said when the thing is found. What it is and what it is for, in the same short diegetic register as the rest of the writing.
itemBlurbs.precept-knife: A monk’s blade, meant for cutting cloth and rope. It has been kept sharp anyway.
itemBlurbs.peachwood-sword: Peach wood takes an edge badly and takes a spirit well.
itemBlurbs.coin-sword: Old coins lashed to a spine of wire. Every emperor on it is dead, which is the point.
itemBlurbs.sevenstar-sword: The Dipper inlaid down the blade. The best iron in the village, and it knows it.
itemBlurbs.truefire-talisman: Yellow paper, red script. Burns on contact and lends its fire to a sword.
itemBlurbs.fivethunder-talisman: Five thunders, folded small. You get one, and it is enormous.
itemBlurbs.blood-talisman: Written in your own. It costs what it says it costs.
itemBlurbs.cinnabar: Ground red mineral. Paint a charm twice and it works twice.
itemBlurbs.soul-banner: The banner the priest would have carried. In your hands a sword swings for two.
itemBlurbs.sticky-rice: Draws 屍毒 out of a wound. Also feeds you, which matters by eleven.
itemBlurbs.black-dog-blood: Thrown, it buys you the doorway. It buys you nothing from the King.
itemBlurbs.golden-elixir: Half of these were made by someone who knew what they were doing.
itemBlurbs.protective-charm: Sewn shut and worn against the skin. It takes the first of every blow.

events._note: One line per event type per hour band, keyed the way events.json is: the `t` value, then 9 / 10 / 11. HP splits by the sign of `hp` — HP_LOSS is 損血, HP_GAIN is 回血 — because one line cannot serve both. The band is the register: nine o'clock is a house settling, eleven is a house with something in it.

JIANGSHI.9: Something in the dark straightens up, and hops.
JIANGSHI.10: They come at the sound of you, stiff-legged and unhurried.
JIANGSHI.11: The room fills with them. They have stopped pretending to be furniture.

HP_LOSS.9: A bad step in the dark. It still costs you.
HP_LOSS.10: Something goes past your face in the dark and takes skin with it.
HP_LOSS.11: The cold in here bites, and takes your breath with it.

HP_GAIN.9: Clean water, and a moment long enough to drink it.
HP_GAIN.10: You find a wall to put your back against, and your breath with it.
HP_GAIN.11: A stub of incense, still warm. You sit until it is out.

NOTHING.10: Dust, and the sound of your own steps.
NOTHING.11: Silence, and the smell of old rain.

POISON.9: A nail catches you. The scratch goes grey at the edges.
POISON.10: Cold fingers brush your wrist, and the cold stays.
POISON.11: 屍毒 is in your blood now. You can feel it looking for your heart.

VILLAGER.9: Someone is still alive in here, and hurt.
VILLAGER.10: A villager, cornered, and not dead yet.
VILLAGER.11: Someone calls out. There is still time to reach them.

eventNames._note: The event types by name, for the log and the turn summary. Keyed by the `t` in events.json, with HP split by sign.
eventNames.VILLAGER: 村民受傷 A villager is hurt

villager._note: The one event that asks a question. Rice buys the stranger; refusing leaves you with what was chasing them.
villager.ask: You have 糯米. Give it, and they may live.
villager.gave: They take it, press {gift} into your hands, and are gone.
villager.refused: You keep the rice. What was behind them is in front of you now.

poison._note: 屍毒 is the substance; 中毒 is the state. The status flag says 中毒; flavour about what is in your blood says 屍毒.
poison.onset: 屍毒. It does not stop on its own.
poison.tick: The grey under your skin creeps a little further.
poison.cured: The 糯米 draws it out. Your hands are your own again.

actions._note: The turn's three choices and the mechanics they touch. Held here so the code keeps using the code term and the screen keeps using the name.

king._note: Midnight and what arrives with it.

setting._note: The place, for flavour text. 屍毒 is the substance and 中毒 the state of having it — see poison.

outcomes._note: How the night ended. WIN_SEAL and WIN_BURIAL must read as equals — same register, same length, neither grander. The seal is the hidden ending, not the better one.
outcomes.WIN_BURIAL: 下葬 The tablet is back in the ground
outcomes.WIN_SEAL: 鎮屍 The paper is on his forehead
outcomes.LOSS_HEALTH: 傷重不治 You did not last the night
outcomes.LOSS_KING: 王帶走了你 The King took you

subs._note: The line under each verdict title. WIN_BURIAL and WIN_SEAL are held to the same register AND the same length on purpose (§9): the seal is the hidden ending, not the better one, and a longer or louder sentence would be the game congratulating you for finding it. Nothing here explains the seal, and nothing anywhere else mentions it.
subs.WIN_BURIAL: You filled the hole in before the light came.
subs.WIN_SEAL: He did not take another step after that.
subs.LOSS_KING: You met him at the third watch, and came up short.

note._note: The first-run letter. Diegetic, in the same voice as the event lines, and it teaches the burial and nothing else: where the tablet is, where it has to go, the one way out of the village, and that the night is short. The King is named as a deadline, never as a second way to win — that ending is hidden and the letter is the last place it should leak.
note.title: A note, folded and left on the gatehouse table
lines: You know why you are here. At the far end of the village is the 義莊, and in it one coffin that has waited too long for anybody to come for it.

His 神主牌 is in the 停柩房. Take it, carry it out through the moon gate in the 天井 — that is the only way out of the village — and put it back in the ground at the 亂葬崗. Give the man his name and he can rest.
Be quick about it. You have from nine until the third watch and not one turn longer. When it sounds he is awake, and he comes to whatever room you are standing in.
Doors are on the walls. Use them.

epilogue._note: Fragments for the one composed sentence on the verdict card. Assembled from the run's own facts and nothing else — no dice, so the same run always ends with the same words. Placeholders: {hour} {weapon} {relic} {goal} {rooms}. NOTE both wins share open.won / open.won-hurt word for word and differ only in the close clause: that is the §9 equal-register rule made structural rather than merely intended. The clauses are joined with `join` and closed with `end`, both themeable: the anticipated per-language ASSEMBLY turned out to be two punctuation marks, because open/hand/close reads the same way round in English and Chinese and `rooms` was already a per-number table, which is measure words already solved.

open.won: You walked out at first light
open.won-hurt: You walked out at first light on your last heart
open.combat-swarmed: They came through the wall at {hour} and did not stop
open.health-worn: The village wore you through by {hour}
open.midnight: The third watch found you still inside
open.king: He came for you at the third watch

close.buried: and the {relic} back in the ground where it belongs
close.carrying-there: the {relic} on you and the {goal} under your feet
close.carrying-far: the {relic} on you and the {goal} still {rooms} away
close.carrying-lost: the {relic} on you and no way through to the {goal}
close.sealed: and the paper still on his forehead where you put it

verdict._note: The verdict card: its title fallbacks and the summary rows beneath. Whole clauses on purpose — word order moves between languages and a template assembled from fragments would only ever be English in disguise.
verdict.lost-fallback: You are one of them now

room._note: The room read aloud, one clause per wall. Each is a complete fragment on purpose: a language that puts the direction after the noun rewrites the template rather than fighting the code.
room.wall-failing: To the {dir}, a wall giving way — they are coming through it.
room.outside: To the {dir}, the arrow door leading outside.

effects._note: What an item does, said on its pack row. Assembled from whichever clauses apply, so each has to stand alone and join with the separator below — a language that punctuates lists differently changes `join` and nothing else.
effects.buff-sword: or +{n} to a sword, for good

tileNotes._note: The tile gallery's plain-words notes, keyed off the same fields the engine reads so a tile cannot gain a power the gallery omits. {tablet} and {room} are filled from this same file.
tileNotes.start-outdoor: Set aside at setup — it goes down the moment you first step outside.
tileNotes.search-weapon: 搜索 Search here for a 武器 weapon.
tileNotes.search-magic: 搜索 Search here for a 符咒 talisman.
tileNotes.search-medicine: 搜索 Search here for 丹藥 medicine.
tileNotes.search-relic: 搜索 Search here for the 法器 — and nowhere else in the village.
tileNotes.moon-gate: Carries the 月門 moon gate — its {dir} way out leads outside the village, not to another room.
tileNotes.seam: Joins the village along its seam edge, the way back in.
tileNotes.take-tablet: The {tablet} is here. Resolve the room's event, then one more for the opening of the coffin. Survive it and still be standing here, and it is yours.
tileNotes.bury-tablet: Break ground, then one more for the digging. Survive that holding the {tablet} and you have won.
tileNotes.heal-1: +1 Health if you end your turn here.
tileNotes.load-failed: Could not load the tile set.
tileNotes.warded: 石敢當 wards this ground: no event is drawn here, entering or staying. The only safety in the village that stays where it is.

tallyLine._note: The line on the menu that says you have been here before. Numbers are spelled out up to twelve — 'four times' is something somebody says, 'Taken: 4' is a statistic, and this is meant to be the former.
tallyLine.left-once: You have walked out of this house once. It has never kept you.
tallyLine.left-many: You have walked out of this house {n}. It has never kept you.

landing._note: The landing page's two pieces of prose. The four charms carry both languages at once by design and the title lockup is a bilingual wordmark, so neither needs a translation — only these do.
landing.tagline: It is nine at night. At the third watch he comes for you. Lay him to rest, or be standing when he arrives.
landing.footnote: A free solo board game in the browser. The rules come from a print-and-play original; the village, the night and everything in it are ours.
